subject: Controlling for variable effort in spAbundance - transect.lenghts vs offset

messages.author: f18889d55d3eefd9
messages.subject: Controlling for variable effort in spAbundance - transect.lenghts vs offset
parts:
Hello!

I'm using the distance sampling function in spAbundance to get transect-level yearly estimates for a 20 year dataset. I've formatted my data so that every row is a transect-year combination and am including year as a covariate in my models to get at overall trends. 
The transects in this case consist of points along a line where point counts were conducted, and in some years not all points were visited. I want to account for this variation in effort and have a few questions:
1. If I supply transect.lengths a vector with the length of each transect that was surveyed, will that effectively take care of effort?
2. Am I correct in thinking that if no offset is supplied, the output will be number of individuals per transect? (or in my case transect-year)
3. I would ultimately like the output to be density per square km to be consistent with prior reports - in order to do this would I have to provide a vector of offset values before fitting models (and what would those be in relation to transect lengths?) or alternatively would I manipulate the model output (N.samples?) to calculate density post hoc?

Thanks a lot!!
Taylor
